description:
## What

In `src/fetcher/dns_cache.cr`, `lookup` deletes expired entries as a side effect of being a read. The pure version: lookup is a read; expired cleanup is `clear_expired`'s job.

## Why

Side effects in a read method make the cache harder to reason about and harder to test (the same input can produce different state across calls). The current behavior is a perf optimization ("clean on read") that mostly hides the periodic cleanup lag.

## Trade-off

Expired entries will persist up to one `PeriodicCleanup` interval (60s by default) after expiration instead of being removed on first lookup. `enforce_limit` might evict fresh entries before expired ones (random eviction doesn't know about expiration). Both effects are small in practice.

## How

In `dns_cache.cr`, change `lookup` from:

```crystal
if entry[:expires] > Time.utc
  entry[:addr]
else
  @@cache.delete(host)
  nil
end
```

to:

```crystal
entry[:expires] > Time.utc ? entry[:addr] : nil
```

Update the docstring to call out the contract: `lookup` is a pure read; expired entries are removed by `clear_expired`.

## Done when

- `lookup` no longer mutates `@@cache`
- Spec `dns_cache_spec.cr` still passes (it asserts on lookup return value, not on cache state)
- Full spec suite still green (415 examples)
title: Refactor: make DnsCache.lookup pure (no delete on expired) (9el.1 follow-up)
